_note: Curated appeal deadlines for the 10 most-populous US states + Indiana. Source: state insurance codes and ACA §2719 implementation. Last verified: 2025-01-01. Web search is the fallback for all other states.

CA.external_review_authority: California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) / California Department of Insurance (CDI)
CA.external_review_statute: Cal. Health & Safety Code §§ 1374.30–1374.34; Cal. Ins. Code § 10169
CA.notes: CA offers Independent Medical Review (IMR) through DMHC for HMO plans and CDI for PPO plans. IMR decisions are binding.

TX.notes: TX requires Independent Review Organizations (IROs) accredited by URAC for external review.

FL.external_review_authority: Florida Department of Financial Services (DFS) / Florida Office of Insurance Regulation (OIR)
FL.notes: Florida external review deadline is 60 days from internal denial. OIR oversees HMO appeals.

NY.external_review_authority: New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS) — External Appeal Program
NY.external_review_statute: N.Y. Ins. Law §§ 4900–4910; N.Y. Pub. Health Law § 4900
NY.notes: NY external appeal must be filed within 45 days of final adverse determination. External appeal is free; independent organization decides within 30 days.

PA.notes: PA external review available for medical necessity and experimental treatment denials.

IL.notes: IL external review deadline is 60 days from final internal adverse determination.

OH.notes: OH external review process available through ODI-certified IROs.

GA.external_review_authority: Georgia Office of Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner
GA.notes: GA external review available for adverse benefit determinations involving medical necessity.

NC.notes: NC external review available for medical necessity and experimental treatment denials.

MI.external_review_authority: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services (DIFS)
MI.notes: MI external review available through DIFS for denials based on medical necessity or experimental treatments.

IN.notes: Indiana external review requires submission within 4 months of final internal adverse determination.
